resources.title: Household water continuity plan
resources.summary: Plan stored supplies, access, containers and source-specific safety decisions.
checklist: Record household members, pets, accessibility needs, planned duration, and the source used for each supply assumption.
Inventory sealed drinking-water supplies by container, quantity, location, purchase date and rotation date.
List normal, backup and emergency collection sources; mark unverified sources as unverified.
Keep the original CDC water documents available offline and printed with the plan.
Record local water authority and health department contacts and a place to log advisories.
Keep chemical contamination questions separate from microbial treatment; do not let a generic treatment plan certify an unknown source.
List containers, labels, cleaning supplies, and who will inspect and rotate each stored supply.
Log measurements, observations and unresolved questions before making a source-specific decision.

resources.title: Food supply and cold-storage plan
resources.summary: Inventory, rotate and plan safe storage and preparation without inventing preservation recipes.
checklist: Record food quantities, lot identifiers, expiry dates, storage locations and packaging condition.
Group foods by dietary needs, allergens, preparation requirements, and available cooking equipment.
Plan menus using foods the household already eats; record the assumptions behind any duration estimate.
Keep refrigerator and freezer temperature records and an outage start-time log.
Use the original FoodSafety.gov outage chart for item-specific decisions rather than a generated table.
Keep tested preservation instructions with their exact edition, ingredient quantities and equipment requirements.
Create rotation, pest inspection and replenishment tasks with named owners.
Keep infant feeding, medical diets and pet food requirements visible as separate inventory requirements.

resources.title: Shelter and evacuation planning card
resources.summary: Document safe places, access needs, evacuation choices and essential supplies.
checklist: List home, nearby and out-of-area meeting places with addresses and contact information.
Record local evacuation and shelter information from the responsible authorities.
Identify transport, accessibility, mobility, language and pet needs for every household member.
Prepare a portable document list and weather-appropriate clothing and bedding inventory.
Identify hazards that require leaving rather than attempting a repair.
Arrange a way to confirm a destination is open before departure when communications allow.
Assign who carries supplies, checks on household members, and reports arrival.
Practice the route and record changes, obstacles and alternate meeting points.

resources.title: Hygiene and waste continuity plan
resources.summary: Plan hygiene, waste separation and lawful disposal when normal services fail.
checklist: Inventory handwashing, personal hygiene, cleaning and waste-storage supplies.
Separate drinking-water containers from cleaning, wastewater and waste containers.
Record household access needs and private facilities for children and dependent adults.
Record municipal or local health department instructions for interrupted sewage and waste collection.
List approved disposal arrangements and who is responsible for contacting service providers.
Keep manufacturer labels and original agency cleaning guidance with supplies.
Avoid mixing cleaning chemicals or treating a household plan as approval for an untested sewage system.
Schedule cleaning, supply checks and documentation of unresolved contamination concerns.

resources.title: Health continuity and care coordination card
resources.summary: Organize personal medical preparedness, contacts, training and continuity of care.
checklist: Keep an owner-controlled list of clinicians, emergency contacts, care providers and preferred facilities.
Record prescriptions, original labels and storage requirements as directed by the prescriber or manufacturer.
Ask the treating clinician about continuity plans for medicines, refrigeration and powered medical devices.
Inventory first-aid supplies and record expiry dates and completed hands-on training.
Document allergies, accessibility requirements and consent for sharing medical information.
Plan transport, caregiver backup and communication support.
Use qualified medical help for diagnosis, treatment and medication changes; this card contains no treatment protocol.
Keep private medical records out of shared exports and general public reference packs.

resources.title: Essential power and backup planning card
resources.summary: Measure essential loads and plan safe backup power and equipment maintenance.
checklist: List essential devices, measured watts, expected daily run time, surge requirements and charging options.
Separate life-critical medical equipment plans from convenience loads and consult its provider.
Record battery capacity, charging losses and actual observed runtime instead of assuming a universal runtime.
Keep the generator manual and original CDC carbon-monoxide document with the power plan.
Arrange qualified review of transfer equipment, wiring, fuel storage and any fixed installation.
Inventory tested alarms, appropriate cables and manufacturer-required maintenance supplies.
Record fuel quantities, inspection dates, operating limits and responsible trained users.
Practice a controlled outage drill, document results and revise the load plan.

resources.title: Garden and growing-system planning card
resources.summary: Maintain a site-specific growing plan, observations, seed inventory and local expertise.
checklist: Record available space, sun exposure, water access, soil observations and local growing conditions.
Keep seed variety, source, lot, storage and planting records.
Consult local extension guidance for region-appropriate crops, planting periods and soil testing.
Start with a manageable trial and record yields, losses, labor, water and inputs.
Plan crop rotation, soil cover and pest monitoring using sources appropriate to the site.
Keep livestock welfare, veterinary needs and legal requirements in a separate plan if animals are involved.
Separate tested food-preservation procedures from garden-production notes.
Do not use historical farm literature as a substitute for current chemical labels or local food-safety guidance.

resources.title: Workshop tools and maintenance register
resources.summary: Inventory maintainable hand tools, measuring equipment, manuals and training.
checklist: Inventory tools, consumables, spare parts, compatible fasteners and storage locations.
Keep manufacturer manuals, inspection requirements and safe operating limits with each tool.
Record who has practical training and which tasks require a qualified specialist.
Check measuring instruments against a suitable reference and record units explicitly.
Separate damaged or unverified equipment from serviceable equipment.
Plan maintenance intervals and replacement parts from actual use and manufacturer guidance.
Record the power, ventilation, guarding and protective equipment needed for each work area.
Use drawings and prototypes for review before committing materials to an unfamiliar build.

resources.title: Materials inventory and reuse assessment
resources.summary: Track safe material identification, compatibility, storage and traceable reuse.
checklist: Record material type, quantity, dimensions, condition, source and any known specification.
Keep labels and safety data sheets with chemicals and commercial materials.
Mark unidentified, contaminated, damaged or degraded materials as unsuitable until assessed.
Separate incompatible storage categories according to verified labels and professional guidance.
Record whether a proposed reuse is decorative, temporary or load-bearing.
Use qualified review for structural, pressure, electrical, potable-water and food-contact uses.
Log test methods, measurements and uncertainty instead of treating appearance as proof of suitability.
Keep a replenishment and disposal plan with local legal and environmental requirements.

resources.title: Household and community communication plan
resources.summary: Maintain contacts, agreed messages, radio documentation and fallback methods.
checklist: Keep printed local and out-of-area contact lists and meeting-place details.
Choose check-in times, a primary contact and a backup contact.
Prepare a short message format for identity, location, needs and next check-in time.
Inventory radios, chargers, batteries, cables and written operating instructions.
Record lawful frequencies, licensing requirements and trained operators for transmitting equipment.
Plan an accessible communication method for people who cannot use the primary method.
Maintain a paper message log with time, sender, recipient and confirmation status.
Test the plan periodically and distinguish confirmed information from rumors.

resources.title: Local map and route planning card
resources.summary: Prepare dated local maps, routes, place names and travel decisions.
checklist: Select maps for the actual area of interest and record source, scale, datum and publication date.
Keep printed route maps and an offline copy that opens without a network connection.
Mark meeting places, known shelters and essential services only from verified information.
Plan alternatives for blocked roads, flood areas, accessibility needs and transport limitations.
Record how coordinates are formatted and check them against recognizable landmarks.
Practice using map and compass with competent instruction before relying on them.
Treat bridge status, road access and weather as changing information that an old map cannot verify.
Carry a travel and check-in plan appropriate to the household and local advice.

resources.title: Repair and construction readiness checklist
resources.summary: Document condition, requirements, approvals and professional review before work.
checklist: Record the problem, photographs, measurements, location and immediate access restrictions.
Separate temporary shelter needs from permanent repair or rebuilding work.
Identify utilities, permits, building-code requirements and responsible authorities.
Arrange qualified inspection for structural damage, foundations, wiring, gas, pressure or fire systems.
List verified materials, tools, costs, dependencies and required skills.
Keep design drawings, assumptions, revisions and inspection outcomes together.
Do not treat a generated CAD drawing or quantity estimate as engineering certification.
Record acceptance criteria and obtain required inspections before putting the work into service.

resources.title: Mutual aid and community coordination card
resources.summary: Coordinate needs, accessible communication, roles and accountable decisions.
checklist: Ask participants what support they need and what they can safely offer.
Document consent, accessibility, privacy and safeguarding expectations.
Assign clear roles for coordination, supplies, communication and record keeping.
Maintain a current resource directory with responsible contacts and verification dates.
Agree how requests are prioritized, confirmed, handed over and closed.
Use existing local emergency coordination arrangements where available.
Keep records of decisions, commitments, donated goods and unresolved needs.
Review the plan with participants and avoid presenting an informal group as a public authority.

resources.title: Skills and reference preservation plan
resources.summary: Preserve skills, reference provenance and safe practical learning.
checklist: Inventory practical skills, available instructors, training records and learning priorities.
Keep offline references with title, author, edition, source URL and rights information.
Prepare printed quick-reference indexes for essential material.
Record observations, hypotheses, methods and results for safe, appropriately supervised experiments.
Distinguish historical descriptions from current tested procedures.
Match learning activities to equipment, supervision and participant ability.
Practice teach-back and record questions that require expert review.
Keep original source documents available so a generated explanation can be checked.

resources.title: Supplies, transport and replenishment register
resources.summary: Track quantities, dependencies, transport, responsibilities and replenishment.
checklist: Create an inventory with item, unit, quantity, location, owner and last verification date.
Separate minimum requirements, preferences and assumptions in each plan.
Use explicit units and measured consumption when estimating how long supplies last.
Record suppliers, alternates, lead times, transport needs and access constraints.
Assign inspection, rotation, maintenance and replenishment tasks.
Track shared resources, commitments, receipts and handovers without exposing private credentials.
Run a small exercise and compare predicted needs with actual use.
Revise the plan after household changes, expired supplies or failed assumptions.

resources.title: Offline knowledge and digital continuity plan
resources.summary: Keep the local assistant, records, backups and reference media usable offline.
checklist: Keep the full Ariadne folder together with the intended local model and reference assets.
Record startup instructions and where the owner pairing key is stored securely.
Verify backup hashes and practice restoring a separate test copy without replacing live owner state.
Keep a printed index of essential contacts and documents for times when the computer cannot run.
Use a measured power budget, suitable backup hardware and manufacturer shutdown instructions.
Keep private databases, books, medical records, keys and credentials out of public distribution packs.
Record software versions, model provenance and document review dates.
Test local search and document access without depending on a hosted service; record the scope and limits of the test.
